title: Maintenance and safety inspection
subtitle: Cleaning your firearm and checking it is safe to fire

lines: In this episode: cleaning your firearm, and carrying out a safety inspection.
The book says the condition of your firearm can mean the difference between life and death.

rule.text: Always unload your firearm before cleaning.

lines: First: always unload your firearm before cleaning.
The firearm is a mechanical device with moving parts, just like any other piece of machinery.
Therefore, if you want it to work reliably, you must keep it clean.

scenes.heading: When to clean the firearm
bullets: It has been used
It has been exposed to the elements
It has been stored for an extended period
lines: The firearm should be thoroughly cleaned every time after three things.

lines.text: One: it has been used.
Two: it has been exposed to the elements, such as sand, mud, rain, sweat or heat.
Three: it has been stored for an extended period.

scenes.caption: Cleaning kit
lines: Your cleaning kit should include a cleaning rod, a phosphor bronze brush, and a jag.
And flannel patches, nitro solvent, and gun oil.

scenes.heading: Cleaning the barrel
bullets: Brush saturated with nitro solvent, ten to twenty times
Solvent-soaked flannel patch on the jag, ten to twenty times
Repeat with a dry patch
lines: When cleaning the barrel, if possible, push the brush down the barrel in the same direction that the bullet will travel.
This prevents unnecessary wear on the barrel.

lines.text: One: saturate the phosphor bronze brush with nitro solvent, and push it through the barrel several times, ten to twenty times.
Two: place a flannel patch around the jag, soak it with nitro solvent, and push the patch through the barrel ten to twenty times.
Three: repeat this last step with a dry patch, to remove the excess solvent from the barrel.

scenes.heading: After cleaning
bullets: Wipe the rest down with gun oil
No oil or solvent left in the barrel
No excessive oil in the magazine or cylinder
A thin coat on slide rails and moving parts

lines.text: The rest of the firearm can be wiped down with gun oil.
After you have cleaned your firearm, make sure there is no oil or solvent left in the barrel.

lines: If there is oil in the barrel and you fire a shot, you can damage the firearm.

lines.text: Also, make sure there is not excessive oil left in the magazine of the pistol, or in the cylinder of the revolver.

lines: This may contaminate the powder and primer of your ammunition.
Excessive oil on the firearm will also attract dirt.

lines.text: It is, however, a good idea to leave a thin coat of oil on the slide rails and moving parts of the firearm.

rule.text: Store the ammunition away from oil and solvent when cleaning your firearm.

lines: If you are going to store your firearm for a long time, leave a coating of oil on the firearm and in the barrel to avoid rust.
However, do not forget to remove the oil from the barrel before firing.
And remember: always store the ammunition away from oil and solvent when cleaning your firearm.
The oil and solvent will attack the primer and contaminate the powder, rendering the ammunition useless, or cause a squib load.

scenes.definition: A quick inspection before firing a gun that has not been used in a long time, to ensure the firearm is safe for firing.
lines: Before firing a gun that has not been used in a long time, one should always carry out a quick safety inspection.
This is to ensure that the firearm is safe for firing.
Never look down the muzzle of an assembled firearm.
To look down the muzzle, you should first strip the firearm.
The book shows you how to carry out a safety inspection without stripping the firearm.

scenes.heading: Pistol safety inspection: steps 1 to 5
bullets: Step 1: Identify a safe direction
Step 2: Safe direction, finger off the trigger
Step 3: Remove the magazine
Step 4: Pull back the slide, pointing safely
Step 5: Check the chamber and the magazine-well
lines: Step one: identify a safe direction.
Step two: point the firearm in a safe direction, with your finger off the trigger.
Step three: remove the magazine.
Step four: pull back the slide, keeping the firearm pointing in a safe direction.
Step five: check inside the chamber and down the magazine-well.

scenes.heading: Pistol safety inspection: steps 6 to 9
bullets: Step 6: Lock the slide to the rear
Step 7: Insert the cleaning rod into the muzzle
Step 8: Rod comes out of the chamber end
Step 9: Attach a patch to remove any oil

lines.text: Step six: lock the slide to the rear, using the slide lock.
Step seven: with the slide locked open, insert the cleaning rod into the muzzle of the firearm.
Step eight: you will see the end of the cleaning rod come out of the chamber end of the barrel.

lines: This will show you that the barrel is free of obstruction or ammunition.

lines.text: Step nine: you can now attach a cleaning patch to remove any oil from the barrel.

scenes.caption: The cleaning rod at the chamber end of the barrel
lines: In the book's photo, the end of the cleaning rod is circled, where it comes out of the chamber end of the barrel.

scenes.heading: Revolver safety inspection
bullets: Identify a safe direction
Point it safely, finger off the trigger
Open the cylinder
Take control with the non-gun hand
Take the cleaning rod from your kit
Insert the cleaning rod into the muzzle
Push until it comes out of the chamber end
Brush or flannel patch to remove excessive oil

lines.text: For a revolver, first identify a safe direction.
Point the firearm in a safe direction, with your finger off the trigger.
Open the cylinder.
Take control of the firearm with the non-gun hand.
Take the cleaning rod from your revolver cleaning kit.
Insert the cleaning rod into the muzzle of the revolver.
Push the cleaning rod up the barrel until you can see it come out of the chamber end of the barrel.
You can now attach the cleaning brush or flannel patch to remove any excessive oil from the barrel.

lines: And make sure there is no ammunition contained in the cylinder during the safety inspection.

lines.say: Firearms come in many sizes and designs, like this Taurus P T fifty-one, a six point three five millimetre pistol with a flip-up barrel.

lines: It is recommended that you never pull back the slide by hand on this particular firearm.
For a safety inspection, you simply look into the barrel through the chamber, to ensure there is no ammunition or obstruction in the barrel.
